topic: Photosynthesis: how a plant turns sunlight, water and air into food
title: How Plants Make Food
subtitle: How leaves cook food from light
objectives: Name the three things a plant needs to make food
Explain that a leaf uses sunlight to cook food
Tell that plants release oxygen we breathe
art_direction: flat vector illustration, soft shadows, warm friendly colors, clean shapes

scenes.title: Your Lunch Is Sunshine
scenes.narration: Look at your sandwich at lunch. The bread and the apple slices. That food started as sunshine falling on a green leaf. How is that possible?
scenes.image_prompt: sunny kitchen table with front centered plate showing a sandwich and apple slices in sharp clear focus, small potted green plant by a bright window behind, warm morning light with no white wash

narration.text: Look at your sandwich at lunch. The bread and the apple slices. That food started as sunshine falling on a green leaf. How is that possible?

scenes.title: Plants Cannot Eat Like You
scenes.narration: You can walk to the fridge. A plant cannot. It has no mouth, no legs, no lunchbox. It stays in one spot all day. So how does it ever get food?
scenes.image_prompt: cheerful kid opening a bright fridge next to a potted green plant rooted in soil under warm sun, side by side view

narration.text: You can walk to the fridge. A plant cannot. It has no mouth, no legs, no lunchbox. It stays in one spot all day. So how does it ever get food?

scenes.title: A Leaf Is a Kitchen
scenes.narration: Sunlight shines down. Water comes up from the roots. Air slips in through tiny doors. The green Leaf mixes all three to cook sweet food.
scenes.image_prompt: big friendly green leaf on a sunny plant stem with roots in soil, bright sun above, water drops near roots, soft air swirls around leaf

narration.text: Sunlight shines down. Water comes up from the roots. Air slips in through tiny doors. The green Leaf mixes all three to cook sweet food.

scenes.title: Food Plus Fresh Air
scenes.narration: First gather the three ingredients. Water, air, and sunlight. Then the leaf changes them. They become food for the plant and oxygen for us to breathe.
scenes.manim_brief: Start with three small icons in a row: water drop, air swirl, sun. Show first formula text below them. Then draw a large arrow growing left to right. Fade in two new icons on the right for sweet food and fresh air. End holding the full change from ingredients to food plus oxygen.

narration.text: First gather the three ingredients. Water, air, and sunlight. Then the leaf changes them. They become food for the plant and oxygen for us to breathe.

scenes.title: What Does a Plant Make?
scenes.narration: Here is a quick check. A plant takes sunlight, water and air. What does it make? Food and oxygen, soil and rocks, or paper and plastic. Think quietly while you decide.
scenes.image_prompt: sunny school garden with big green leaves, curious kids looking closely at a plant in bright daylight

quiz.question: A plant takes sunlight, water and air. What does it make?
quiz.explanation: The leaf cooks food for the plant and releases oxygen we breathe.

narration.text: Here is a quick check. A plant takes sunlight, water and air. What does it make? Food and oxygen, soil and rocks, or paper and plastic. Think quietly while you decide.

reveal.text: Food and oxygen. The leaf cooks food for the plant and releases oxygen we breathe.

scenes.title: Leaves Cook With Light
scenes.narration: So remember. Plants turn sunlight, water and air into food. And they share oxygen we breathe in. What green plant near your home would you like to watch in the sun?
scenes.image_prompt: sunny windowsill with several small green potted plants in warm morning light, child watching the leaves

narration.text: So remember. Plants turn sunlight, water and air into food. And they share oxygen we breathe in. What green plant near your home would you like to watch in the sun?

checks.question: 1. Would someone stop?
checks.reason: First frame shows a recognizable sandwich and plant with counterintuitive claim that lunch started as sunshine.

checks.question: 2. Would they want to start the lesson?
checks.reason: Title How Plants Make Food is understandable with zero prior knowledge and key words fit in 40 characters.

checks.question: 3. Would someone watch the video?
checks.reason: Scenes 2, 4, 5 and 6 have null image_prompt and no manim_brief, creating long static text-only stretches.
checks.fix: Add image_prompt / manim_brief and a visual change for every scene so no scene is text-only for more than 3s; e.g. animate fridge vs rooted plant, water moving up, air entering leaf, formula building step-by-step.

checks.question: 4. Would they participate?
checks.reason: Final question about what green plant near your home you would watch plus in-video quiz is answerable from personal experience.

checks.question: 5. Will they be satisfied?
checks.reason: Hook promise how food can start as sunshine is fulfilled inside by water+air+sunlight to food+oxygen explanation.

checks.question: 6. Would they watch it again?
checks.reason: Evergreen core process of three ingredients to food and oxygen works as reference to rewatch, not expiring news.

checks.question: 7. Would they come back for more?
checks.reason: Ending gives summary only with no named concrete next lesson or reason to return.
checks.fix: Add a concrete next-lesson hook in the last line named by curiosity, e.g. Next: why are leaves green and not black to catch more sun?

fact_issues: Summary bullet 'We breathe out fresh oxygen' is backwards: plants release oxygen, humans breathe oxygen in and breathe carbon dioxide out.
Hook claim that cheese in the sandwich 'started as sunshine falling on a green leaf' overstates direct origin: cheese comes from animal milk and is only indirect via cow eating plants.

video_review.summary: This is a clear, accurate and age appropriate introduction to how plants make food. Visuals match the voice throughout, language is simple, and pacing is calm for Grade 5. The quiz and closing question work. Only small timing and clarity tweaks are needed.
strengths: Strong hook that links lunch to sunshine and keeps attention for ages 10 to 11.
Narration and on screen text stay in sync, with each ingredient highlighted as it is named.
Simple kitchen metaphor and clear plant diagram make an abstract process concrete.
Quiz works well with three distinct options, quiet think time, and clear visual feedback with explanation.
Closing summary repeats the three inputs and two outputs and ends with a personal observation prompt.

notes.issue: At about 0:40 both formulas are visible at once. The old water plus air plus sunlight line stays faded above the new box, which can confuse Grade 5 readers.
notes.fix: Remove the faded grey input line when the full arrow formula appears, so only water plus air plus sunlight arrow food plus oxygen is shown large and centered for a few seconds.

notes.issue: At about 0:58 an 8 second countdown appears in the corner with no warning. Eight seconds is short for slower readers to read the question and three options.
notes.fix: Add a voice cue such as You have 12 seconds to think, make the number larger, and hold the three options without other movement until the timer ends.

notes.issue: At about 1:21 the closing question What green plant near your home would you like to watch in the sun appears only at the very end and leaves little time to process it.
notes.fix: After the narration ends, hold the Leaves Cook With Light summary plus the question box silently on screen for at least 5 seconds so students can read and think.
